submitted.rationale: Index 167 (Cr 0.106, Fe 0.709, V 0.185) had the highest measured EQE, 0.077%, out of 3 measurements. MACE puts FeVO4 on the hull, but the film nearest FeVO4 (index 76) gave only 0.051%. The Fe-rich Cr-alloyed region did better. MEGNet puts that region's gap near or below 2.06 eV, so it should absorb these photons.

rejected.reason: Measured 0.051% EQE. This film is close to FeVO4, which is stable, but its EQE was lower than index 167.
Measured 0.052% EQE. Adding a little more Cr and removing some V lowered EQE compared with index 167.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts FeVO4 on the hull (Ehull 0), so it should form at Fe:V≈1. The MEGNet HSE gap is 2.75 eV. HSE usually overestimates this; the experimental FeVO4 gap is about 2.0 eV, close to the 2.06 eV photons. Index 76 (Fe 0.456, V 0.459, Cr 0.085) is the closest low-Cr match to FeVO4.

Weak support, since this is a hypothetical structure. The Fe–Cr oxide (V replaced by Cr) has a MEGNet HSE gap of about 2.0 eV, below the 2.06 eV photons, so it should absorb. The FeVO4-like film gave only 0.05% EQE, so I'm moving to the Fe-rich corner (index 167, Fe 0.71). There, Fe2O3-type phases with some Cr/V should absorb better.

Weak support. The MEGNet GLLB gap for the Fe–Cr oxide is 1.1 eV (HSE earlier gave 2.0 eV), so Fe-rich Cr-alloyed oxides should absorb the 2.06 eV photons. Measured EQE rose from 0.051% at the FeVO4 composition to 0.077% at Fe 0.71. Index 180 (Fe 0.70, V 0.17) continues that trend toward Fe-rich, low-V compositions and is next to the best point so far. The GP top pick (190) is in the same area.
